commenti.body: Oh my god I hated *The Substance* so much. I just saw it and it gave me the same vibe of Men and Maligant but even worse. I wrote down all my thoughts on it before diving into any reviews because I don't want to be swayed or to forget them...I think it'll get the same treatment of Malignant of people labeling a beyond bad movie as camp and loving it due to the over the top visual spectacle and showering it with praise due to the sensation completely disregarding the rough substance.
If you don’t mind me asking, why did it agitate you so much?

I have so so many thoughts but I'll try to be concise, I have some more personal indirect thoughts separated out following these direct points. 

The movie should have probably ended in the first half of the film. Shots and editing were all over the place (still far away shot randomly at the beginning but then excessively using close up shaky cam looking up at the main character rather than a basic medium shot of them walking even if you want to convey stress); overall both the camera movement and the editing reflect a lack of art direction. The writing was poor, the two primary characters did things at one point that directly do not make sense to the character (like antithetical to them, not in a "the character was confused!" way, like..."these shots look sick! let's do that!" vibe). The "message" of the plot misses the mark to the point of making the "commentary" really just portrayal...which...is worse than failure....because you have audiences walking away citing commentary but that's just getting more eyes on something that perpetuates the things that it's trying to demonstrate is bad. The second half of the film feels like if someone started painting Starry Night and then kept going with the stars to the point of making them big circles of yellow on the painting, then started making cartoonish five pointed stars using highlighter over those painted stars...you had something good there and you overshot it and then re-shot that out of the galaxy. It's really upsetting to me when this happens with horror because people feel emotions or have reactions to the gore or whatever and then come out of the theater citing it as a good movie, and then that can put off ambivalent viewers from these genres. Even with all of this, the gore itself was like if you watched a Cronenberg movie and then immediately did a Pictonary drawing of your idea of body horror, it felt like it didn't produce anything new or unique warranting me being in a movie theater watching this happen. Then it basically falls into more nonsense and during the gore sequences the runtime of the scenes almost competes for the level of offense to the scenes and there's issues with the music and audio levels....I'll stop there. It's a lot. 


-- personal thoughts below -- 

Films require a lot of eyes on them, many people working on them, and seeing the story, seeing it come together, reviewing and revising the final product. I just flat out don't think a film should be in a theater if it has such a significant issue with something like not ending when it (likely) should have. 

I get deeply annoyed when I see films like this because it's a reminder that bad films can be mass produced, and I know there's so much very good art out there that's not being seen by a theatrical audience, that doesn't have what I'd say are fundamental or basic issues. 

It's a reminder that in spite of the entire sea of "amateur" artwork or less well known films...what my time and money gets spent on doesn't always meet basic bars of quality of the experience, due to societal and economic issues. 

I know this probably sounds out there but that's honestly genuinely how I feel when I walk out of the theater from this sort of a film, because it technically looks good. This is what struck me the most, combined with all the run of the mill stuff I mentioned at the top of this comment.

Interesting, I absolutely hated Malignant but I really liked The Substance. Not at all without flaws but I thought it was a really enjoyable watch. Me personally, I just love to see a movie dividing people so much. It’s great to see so many vastly different opinions and perspectives on one movie.
Have any of you seen "The Best of Youth"? I just found out about today, but it sounds intriguing. What are your spoiler free thoughts if so, regarding this 6 hour behemoth?

>Films require a lot of eyes on them, many people working on them, and seeing the story, seeing it come together, reviewing and revising the final product. I just flat out don't think a film should be in a theater if it has such a significant issue with something like not ending when it (likely) should have.

Of course I don't know what's going on in the movie business, but is this not the expected result of allowing "auteuristic" visions?  Whether or whether not Fargeat got >90% of what she expected, it must have been right there in the script how the film ended or didn't end. 

That's not to say I disagree with you, but it's hard for me to get worked up on some of these higher budgeted supposed "arthouse" films. I was skeptical from the beginning and ended up passing on it due to reading particular reviews. Ahh, who am I bullshitting, I haven't seen it, why do I get to pretend I should be aloud to have an opinion on *The Substance.* But on the real though, audiences really got some bad taste these days, it's hard to sift through everything. But I don't feel too down on it all.  I sympathize with you.

I've had a few film courses over the years, and being able to provide editing and find a new digital form for something that I have a passion for would be great for this project! :)
